title: Banwari Trace
description: Hunter-gatherers leave the oldest known site in the Caribbean, when Trinidad was still joined to South America.

title: Columbus names Trinidad
description: On his third voyage Columbus sights the island's three hills and names it for the Trinity.

title: San José de Oruna founded
description: Antonio de Berrío founds the island's Spanish capital, the start of a thin colonial presence that lasts two centuries.

title: Courlanders land at Tobago
description: Settlers from the Duchy of Courland on the Baltic plant a colony at Tobago and trade there until the Dutch finally expel them.

title: French take Tobago
description: Tobago falls to the French in the American war, one of many times the island changes hands before the British keep it in 1803.

title: British take Trinidad
description: Spanish governor Chacón capitulates without a fight to a British fleet, ending nearly three centuries of Spanish rule.

title: Spain formally cedes the island
description: Under the Treaty of Amiens Spain cedes Trinidad to Britain for good.

title: First Indian indentured ship
description: The Fatel Rozack lands the first Indian indentured labourers in the Caribbean, remaking the island's population.

title: Tobago joined to Trinidad
description: Britain merges failing Tobago into the Trinidad colony as a ward, creating the single administrative unit that becomes one country.

title: Butler riots
description: The arrest of the strike leader Tubal Uriah Butler triggers island-wide riots and births the modern labour movement.

title: Williams founds the PNM
description: The historian Eric Williams launches the People's National Movement, which rules the country for thirty unbroken years.

title: West Indies Federation formed
description: The Trinidad-based capital news welcomes the new West Indies Federation, which Jamaican withdrawal later dooms.

title: Independence
description: Trinidad and Tobago becomes an independent state within the Commonwealth, Williams as its first prime minister.

title: Black Power Revolution
description: Mass marches against racial inequality end in an army mutiny and hundreds of arrests, forcing social change.

title: Republic
description: Trinidad and Tobago becomes a republic and replaces the British monarch with a president.

title: NAR lands the election
description: A.N.R. Robinson's alliance sweeps out the PNM after thirty years, the first change of government in independent history.

title: Coup attempt
description: Jamaat al Muslimeen storm parliament and take the prime minister hostage for six days; Port of Spain burns in the looting.

title: First female prime minister
description: Kamla Persad-Bissessar is sworn in as the country's first female prime minister.
